text:
[title] Result: 2.4x more requests per second
[body] Same hardware: 8 GPUs, same latency target
[body] Median response time unchanged
[body] Measured on a real chat workload

novice.takeaway: Using the same hardware and keeping response time the same, the presenter's changes let the system handle 2.4x more requests per second in a real chat test.
questions: What counts as 'real chat workload' exactly?
Was latency measured at average or worst-case?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their improvements deliver real, measurable efficiency gains without hurting speed.

peer.takeaway: On the same 8-GPU hardware and latency target, the described techniques achieved 2.4x higher request throughput without hurting median response time, validated on a real chat workload.
questions: How does 'requests per second' relate to earlier p99 latency metric?
What counts as 'real chat workload' specifically?
Is median response time the same metric as p99 latency?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their combined techniques deliver a validated, real-world 2.4x throughput gain at no latency cost.

expert.takeaway: The presenter reports a measured 2.4x throughput gain on identical hardware and latency SLO, tested on a real chat workload, validating the earlier claim.
questions: Is throughput measured at p50, p99, or aggregate RPS?
What is the actual latency target value used?
What request/output length distribution defines 'real chat workload'?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to accept the 2.4x throughput claim as empirically validated under fair conditions.

metrics.intent: Our serving system delivers 2.4x higher goodput at p99 latency by pairing PagedAttention-style KV-cache management with speculative decoding.
